CombatPanel.title: Combat Actions
CombatPanel.grappleTargetHint: Grapple targets the creature you have targeted, and refuses unless that is exactly one (pg 126). Escape takes no target — it rolls against whoever is holding you. Shift-click for advantage, Ctrl-click for disadvantage.
CombatPanel.grappledState: Grappled (pg 134): you cannot spend AP to move. Nothing but an Escape ends it — the book names no other trigger, so nothing here watches for one.
CombatPanel.restrainedState: Restrained (pg 135): you cannot move, and damage you take cannot be subtracted from your stamina points. Escape ends a restraint too (pg 126).
CombatPanel.heldWithoutRecord: Something is holding you that no Grapple recorded — a restraint, a trap, or a Clasp weapon (pg 61, 80, 81). Escape will ask for a DC, because pg 126 prices it off a creature's Unarmed skill and none of those is a creature.
CombatPanel.notHeld: Nothing is holding you: no Grapple recorded a grappler, and neither the grappled nor the restrained status is set. Escape frees you from "a grapple, restrain, or chokehold" (pg 126) and there is none to roll against.
CombatPanel.escapeDcHint: pg 126 sets the DC at 10 + the creature's Unarmed skill, and a trap or a rope has none. The book answers that with a bespoke DC per object — pg 80's bear trap prints "a Strength ability check equal to 15" to pry it open — so the GM names one here. Clasp (pg 61) still describes this roll in v2.0's vocabulary; read as disadvantage on the pg 126 check, which is the only reading that leaves the property doing anything.
CombatPanel.helpNoTarget: Target the ally you are helping first (pg 127).
CombatPanel.helpPick: Related skill — your bonus, and the half your ally receives
CombatPanel.helpHint: v2.1 replaced advantage with a number: the creature you aid adds half your bonus in the related skill, rounded down, to their next check (pg 127). The book prints no floor, so a negative bonus hands your ally a penalty. The attack branch takes no skill and is the half v2.1 did not change — advantage on your ally's first attack roll before your next turn.
CombatPanel.helpTargetHint: Help targets the creature you have targeted, and refuses unless that is exactly one. 6 AP either way (pg 126).
CombatPanel.helpHeldCheck: +{bonus} on your next roll. Spent by the next roll you make, and by nothing else — the book says "their next ability check", which is a trigger and not a clock.
CombatPanel.helpHeldAttack: Advantage on your first attack roll. The book's window closes at the helper's next turn (pg 127), which is a deadline about somebody else's turn — honour it at the table.
CombatPanel.readyCost: The readied action's own AP (a further {surcharge} AP is added)
CombatPanel.readyNeedsTrigger: Ready needs a trigger and an AP cost: pg 126 says "you must specify what the trigger is and spend the necessary AP with an additional 2 AP".
CombatPanel.fireHint: The trigger occurred, so the action happens and no AP comes back (pg 126).
CombatPanel.lapseHint: The trigger never occurred: half the committed AP recycles at the start of your next turn (pg 126). New in v2.1 — v2.0 gave back nothing. Press it after your turn has ended, which is both when the refund is paid and the only moment you can honestly know the trigger never came.
CombatPanel.readyRefund: If none of this fires, {refund} AP recycle at the start of your next turn (pg 126).
CombatPanel.readyRefundDazed: Nothing recycles: a dazed creature cannot recycle AP (pg 133), and Ready's refund is a recycle (pg 126). Neither rule cites the other; this is the reading that leaves both meaning something.
CombatPanel.readyMultiple: More than one action is readied, and Ready resolves per creature rather than per marker — either control here clears every one of them and settles the refund on the total.
